messages.author: 3f37be0cf708d442
messages.subject: speeding up zero inflation model through vectorization?
parts:
Hello,

in the stan language reference a zero inflation model is described as follows:

for (n in 1:N) {
  if (y[n] == 0)
    increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(bernoulli_log(1,theta),
                                                     bernoulli_log(0,theta)
                                                     + poisson_log(y[n],lambda)));
  else
    increment_log_prob(bernoulli_log(0,theta)
                                 + poisson_log(y[n],lambda));
}

I was thinking of improving the speed of the model by
- splitting the array y in two parts, 
  one where y = 0 and the other where y != 0
- putting the results of
  log_sum_exp(bernoulli_log(1,theta),
                      bernoulli_log(0,theta)
                      + poisson_log(y[n],lambda))
  and
  bernoulli_log(0,theta) + poisson_log(y[n],lambda)
  into two vectors log_prob_y and log_prob_y0
- and finally pass the vectors log_prob_y 
  and log_prob_y0 to increment_log_prob

The underlying idea is to vectorize as much as possible. 
For example when calculating log_prob_y and log_prob_y0, 
I would "vectorize" for bernoulli_log and poisson_log or 
neg_binomial_2_lo_log. The only place where one would
still have to loop is for log_sum_exp.

I am unsure if such a modification would would improve 
the speed noticeable, because if I understand it correctly 
calculating the gradients is the most time consuming operation,
and I do not understand if the changes I suggested have any 
influence on the calculation of gradients.


Thanks in advance!
Guido

PS: In my particular case the data set is moderately large
(N = 50 000 rows and 20 predictors) and I am using the 
negative binomial model. 
An improvement in speed of 10% would already be useful for me!

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] speeding up zero inflation model through vectorization?
parts:
I am following up with 2 points:

 

1) My belief that the reference manual describes

and incorrect optimized hurdle model is strengthened

2) Code for a faster zero inflated negative binomial model.

 

### 1) The reference manual describes an ###

###      incorrect optimized hurdle model ###

 

Following up on my last message:

I checked and, as described in the manual,

poissonCDF(0 | lambda) = log(1-exp(-lambda)).

However, to calculate p(y[n] | lambda) for the hurdle model, 

one has to divide (or subtract on the log scale) by the

complementary poisson CDF. poissonCCDF.

Instead, the code on page 115 of the 

reference manual uses the poissonCDF.

 

So it should not be 

increment_log_prob(-log1m_exp(-lambda))

but

increment_log_prob(-log1m_exp(log1m_exp(-lambda))).

[Alternatively, I am making a fool out of myself ...]

 

### 2) Code for a faster zero inflated ###

###      negative binomial model. ###

 

Replacing the model section from page 114 in the 

stan reference the following makes gradient evaluation

ca. 20% faster.

 

This code is for a hierarchical model involving multiple

groups, using following variables:

y: vector of length N with observed counts.

phi: vector with over dispersion parameters for groups

etas: vector of length N containing log(mu) for the negative binomial distribution

thetas: logit of p(y == 0)

sx: design matrix

sx0: design matrix for zero inflation

g_start: index of the first entry for a group in y, sx, or sx0

g_nzstart: index of the first nonzero entry for a group in y, sx, or sx0

g_end: index of the last entry for a group in y, sx, or sx0

betas: matrix with regression weights to obtain log(mu), by group

alphas: regressions weight for zero inflation part (same for all groups)


### begin model ###

...

thetas <- to_vector(sx0 * to_matrix(alpha));

 

for (gr in 1:M) {

    log_phi <- log(phi[gr]);

     etas[g_start[gr]:g_end[gr]] <- sx[g_start[gr]:g_end[gr],1:K] * beta[gr,1:K]';

 

     // y > 0  cases

     increment_log_prob(bernoulli_logit_log(0,thetas[g_nzstart[gr]:g_end[gr]])

                                   + neg_binomial_2_log_log(y[g_nzstart[gr]:g_end[gr]],

                                                                         etas[g_nzstart[gr]:g_end[gr]],

                                                                         phi[gr]));

     // y == 0 cases

     for (k in g_start[gr]:(g_nzstart[gr]-1)) {

       increment_log_prob(log_sum_exp(bernoulli_logit_log(1,thetas[k]),

                                                         bernoulli_logit_log(0,thetas[k]) 

                                                         + neg_binomial_2_log_log(0,etas[k],phi[gr])));            

     }

   }

 

### end model ####


Following additional modifications did make the model

 slightly faster (around 5%), but appeared to be less stable 

(i.e. produced NaNs or infinite values where the above model did not):


bernoulli_logit_log(1,thetas[k]) can be obtained from log_inv_logit(thetas[k])

bernoulli_logit_log(0,thetas[k]) can be obtained from log1m__inv_logit(thetas[k])

neg_binomial_2_log_log(0,etas[k],phi[gr]) can be obtained from

(log1m_exp(etas[k] - log_sum_exp(etas[k],log_phi)))*phi[gr])).


Best, Guido

PS: getting the count of zero values to then use the binomial 
distribution does not work in my case, because every participants
has a different theta value.

Hi Bob,
thanks for your feedback and help!

I am attaching 3 files:
1) HZAxNB2Regression.stan 
is a hierarchical zero inflated negative binomial model 
(hierachical only for the count part, not the the zero inflation part).

2) sim_nbinom_data.R 
simulates zero inflated data and returns those 
and design matrix and parameters used to 
created these data

3) test_HZAxNB2Reg.R
used files 1) and 2) to do a parameter recovery 
test and plot the results.

I think the estimated are close enough to the 
generative parameters, expect that 
I am not able to fully recover the zero alteration 
(which is more a hurdle model ...).
